name: ChoralRoot
author: Quixotic7
description: A Telepathic Orchid-style chord instrument: one hand plays roots, the other shapes chords; voicings, performance modes, bass and a looper.

name: Dinghy
author: zvenson
description: Your base for your own FM-1 firmware: everything under it done and documented (updates, USB rescue, USB-MIDI, USB audio, keys, screen, settings), a 4-voice sine on top.

name: Felucca
author: Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments)
description: The custom firmware the others build on: the FM-1's own synth engines, a sequencer, effects and a better panel, with an editor in the browser.

name: Felucca [Salt]
author: Chance Roth (ChanceTheMaker)
description: Felucca with a hardware-inspired Studio in the browser (play it there without an FM-1): many engines, presets, skins.

name: FiMba-1
author: jadamsowers
description: A physically modelled kalimba: tines laid out like the real one, thumb-roll chords, mbira patterns, a sound hole to cover, grains, tape and a plate reverb.

name: fm1-chord
author: math0ne
description: A chord machine after the HiChord, with extras: chords in a key under the white keys, slash chords and inversions, sounds, envelopes, effects and a looper.

name: FoMni
author: Charles Vestal
description: A chord harp inspired by the Omnichord: strum the white keys, pick chords on the black ones.

name: FuMi-1
author: cartesive
description: A shigin conductor after the Suiko ST-50: its two rows of keys, the key set in honsū, equal or its own just tuning, a koto and twelve more sounds on a 6-op FM engine, ring time, vibrato, trill and a looper.

name: GHOULBOX
author: Jason Persinger
description: Dungeon synth: DREAM composes and evolves ambient pieces from your sounds, a cathedral hall reverb, tape and crush, a hurdy-gurdy engine, choirs, organs and recorded psaltery and harp, an old-RPG screen with wall torches.

name: Hortator
author: DEADACTIVE
description: A drum machine: eight tracks of drums, a step sequencer, Grids, a pumping compressor, LFOs, resonators and live effects.

name: Jangada
author: zednaked
description: Dark, industrial, Brazilian: drones that breathe, ten engines (6-op FM, a superwave analog with a ladder filter), four tracks, a mod matrix, live effects.

name: JIANT FM
author: juanjiant-bit
description: A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings in thermal colours, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice…), mutating macros, song mode from SLOOP.

name: MAKU
author: okumurari
description: An ambience machine for DJ interludes: switch it on and a random world in key plays, four parts, buttons that are verbs, and the worlds you like breed new ones.

name: Melodee
author: keremimo
description: Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.

name: Rainbow Mode
author: joshbartlettband-web
description: A music toy for little children: 63 cartoon friends, every key in tune, chords, strumming, songs to follow and an ear game, notes on a staff, a volume cap for small ears.

name: SLOOP
author: isod89
description: A live groovebox: tracks, layers, a step sequencer, song mode, punch-in effects and samples, played on the FM-1 in real time.

name: SLOOP DX7 Banks
author: majnikool
description: SLOOP 2.4 with up to twelve DX7 voice banks, kept and named in the editor, presets by kind.

name: SLOOP Floyd FM
author: René Bohne
description: SLOOP with a visual four-operator FM engine after Floyd Steinberg's 4-OP idea: an ADSR per operator, seven pages, a live oscilloscope that draws the envelopes as you play.

name: sloopDX
author: zvenson
description: SLOOP's live workflow with Dexed's DX7 engine and 128 steps a track: six operators, 32 algorithms, your own .syx banks, every voice edited on the FM-1, FM drums you program.

name: WaveLoop FM-1
author: ELI7VH
description: Felucca played from an Arturia MiniLab 3: track faders, a DJ filter, momentary effect pads; 32 patches a bank, 12 evolving songs, revoiced 808 and CR78 kits.

name: X0X
author: Charles Vestal
description: A groovebox: 909 and 808 drums, two 303s with TB-3PO, a breakbeat generator and song mode.

name: zp12
author: zvenson
description: A standalone 12-bit sampler inspired by the E-mu SP-1200: sample in the browser (mic, line-in or a file), unplug, and the FM-1 plays on its own: nothing smoothed, loops and songs.
